Fully open-source.** [![GitHub Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/kaomei/stickman-video-director?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/kaomei/stickman-video-director/stargazers) ![MIT License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-16a34a?style=flat-square) Start with a topic, an article, or a script. Automatically orchestrate visuals, voiceovers, captions, and sound effects into a production-ready stickman video. **⚡ 100% Free & Open-Source. ## 🎬 Two ways to make your video **Want control over every shot? Choose A · Director Mode. Want a finished video without assembling scenes yourself? Choose B · Autopilot Mode.** One project, two workflows. | |
A · Director Mode
|
B · Autopilot Mode
| |:---:|:---|:---| | **Approach** | **You control production; AI plans the shots.** Get storyboards and prompts, then generate clips and edit them yourself. | **Give it a topic or a brief; get a finished video.** Automate illustrations, voiceover, captions, subtle animation, and video assembly. | | **Length** | **Short-first**, typically 30 seconds–3 minutes. Longer videos can be built scene by scene. | **Long-form-first**, especially narrated videos of **10 minutes or more**. Also works for shorts and episodic stories. | | **Tools** | Plan with a Skill-compatible AI assistant, generate clips in your preferred video generator (Google Flow, Runway, Luma, Kling, etc.), then assemble in CapCut or Premiere. | Run in **Codex, Claude Code**, or another AI coding agent that can read and write files, call tools, and execute commands to connect generation with local rendering. | | **Visuals** | **Generated animated clips**, with character movement, camera direction, and interactions. | **Illustrated scenes with subtle animation**, using cuts, pans, and zooms to support the narration rather than generating a full-motion clip for every scene. | | **Output** | A director's treatment, storyboards, scene-by-scene video prompts, and sound design. | **A complete video file with voiceover, captions, and subtle animation.** | | **Start** |
Use Director Mode
|
Use Autopilot Mode
| Both workflows can start with a raw topic, a web link, or a full script. Customize your aspect ratio (9:16, 16:9, 1:1), narration language, and voiceover freely. The lengths above are recommendations, not hard limits. 💡 **Quick Setup Note**: - **Director Mode** works anywhere in standard conversational AI windows. - **Autopilot Mode** runs inside AI coding agents with file/terminal access (like **Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, or Cursor**) to automatically handle end-to-end rendering and file delivery. ## 🧭 Get started Compatible with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Antigravity, or any agent environment with file/terminal access. Send the following to your AI assistant: ```text Install this Skill for me: https://github.com/kaomei/stickman-video-director Once installed, read the installed SKILL.md right away. Explain what each mode produces, the tools it needs, and the workflow in plain language, with examples I can copy. Based on what I want to make, tell me what is missing and exactly what to do next. ``` ### A · Director Mode: scene-by-scene video prompts After installation, send this to your AI assistant and replace the placeholder with your topic: ```text Use Director Mode / mode A to turn the following topic, copy, or brief into a stickman video: [Enter a topic, paste your copy, or describe what you need] Requirements: landscape 16:9, A3 "Prehistoric Cave" style, starting with 30 seconds. Give me the director's treatment first. After I approve it, provide scene-by-scene video prompts. ``` **Workflow: share your topic and brief → develop the story script → optionally approve front, side, and back character views → generate detailed storyboard prompts → manually generate clips and edit the final video** The treatment covers the story structure, scene-by-scene narration, actions, camera direction, and sound design. Copy each prompt into [Google Flow](https://flow.google.com/) or another video generator, then add captions and finish the edit in CapCut or your preferred editor. For your first video, follow the [visual production walkthrough on X](https://x.com/CrazyKaomei/status/2102311241046008268) (Thread with step-by-step video demos). ### B · Autopilot Mode: from a brief to a long-form video After installing in Codex, Claude Code, or another environment with file access and command execution, try: ```text Use Autopilot Mode / mode B to turn the following topic, article, post, news item, or brief into a compelling YouTube video: [Paste content or a link, or describe what you want to promote] Requirements: 5–10 minutes, landscape 16:9, B1 "Minimal Hand-Drawn" style, with voiceover, captions, and sound effects. Check the image generation, voiceover, and video-rendering setup first. Then give me a script and a 20-second preview with sound. After I approve it, build the full video with visuals timed to the narration. Deliver a complete video file; I do not want to assemble scenes myself. ``` **Workflow: share a topic, content, or brief → approve the script → approve a 20-second preview with sound → automatically produce the full video → receive the finished video file** The AI assistant plans the scenes, generates the visuals and narration, adds captions and sound effects, and renders a complete video to the voiceover's timing. You approve the script and preview; you do not have to generate and assemble every scene yourself. On first use, it checks the required setup and walks you through anything missing. If a visual or voiceover section needs work, revise just that section and keep what you have already approved. ## 🎨 A · Director Mode style gallery Styles are numbered A1, A2, A3… Each includes its own animated examples. ### A1: Classic Black & White Explain an idea with just a few lines. On a pure white or black canvas, characters, props, and a little accent color do the heavy lifting—ideal for brisk, clear explainers. - **Visual style**: simple round heads, line-drawn limbs, and consistent stroke widths, with occasional simple expressions. Up to three saturated accent colors signal emotion, risk, or action. Abstract ideas become visual metaphors: anxiety as a cage, attention as a progress bar. - **Best for**: science explainers, psychology, motivation, self-management, business breakdowns, and abstract concepts. - **Choose your look**: black characters on white feel clean and direct for teaching and everyday explainers. White characters on black create stronger contrast for suspense, conflict, and emotion. | A1.1 · Black on white | A1.2 · White on black | |:---:|:---:| | | | | Pure white canvas · Black characters | Pure black canvas · White characters | --- ### A2: Modern Pop A red beanie and yellow T-shirt give this character an instantly recognizable look. Explain a product in a clean tech setting, or follow the character into bedrooms, city streets, and the wilderness for a story with real ups and downs. - **Visual style**: a minimalist character with a consistent red beanie and yellow shirt, in two types of setting. Minimal Tech pairs white space and a faint grid with floating glass-like interfaces and cyan light. Colorful Story uses richer scenery, lighting, and depth to set the mood. - **Best for**: Minimal Tech suits AI tools, tech products, tutorials, and feature walkthroughs. Colorful Story works for personal growth, everyday life, adventure, and motivational stories. - **Choose your look**: explaining a tool or method? Pick Minimal Tech. Taking viewers through a character's experience? Pick Colorful Story. | A2.1 · Minimal Tech | A2.2 · Colorful Story | |:---:|:---:| | | | | White space · Faint grid · Cyan glow | Colorful scenes · Cinematic lighting · Story atmosphere | --- ### A3: Prehistoric Cave Take today's problems back to a world without phones or offices. Caves, animal skins, campfires, and exaggerated expressions turn the absurdities of work and human nature into short stories with a twist. - **Visual style**: bold hand-drawn strokes, solid white heads, dark limbs, animal-skin clothing, and earthy surroundings. Character interactions, reaction shots, and comic pauses drive the story. Design the cast for each story—different ages and genders are welcome; not every story needs the same face. - **Best for**: prehistoric what-ifs, workplace satire, observations on human nature, dark comedy, fables, and English-learning stories for children. - **Choose this when**: a small story needs an “aha” moment or an unexpected turn. Modern relationships transplanted into a prehistoric tribe make for jokes that feel both familiar and surprising. | Example 1: "How Did Humans Get Their First Job?" | Example 2: "The First Discovery of Fire" | |:---:|:---:| | | | | Prehistoric story · Workplace twist | Discovery of fire · Community creation | --- ### A4: Cozy Storytelling A mug too special to use. A message you feel you have to answer immediately. An afternoon finally kept for yourself. Simple characters inhabit colorful everyday settings, telling relatable stories through movement, expressions, and camera work. - **Visual style**: solid white round heads, slim bodies, fine dark limbs, and natural expressions in fully illustrated 2D environments. Wide shots establish the setting, close-ups capture hesitation or relief, and tracking shots follow the character forward. - **Best for**: relatable everyday stories, personal growth, relationships, heartwarming moments, habit-building, and English-learning content for children. - **Choose this when**: you want viewers to recognize themselves in a small moment. Adapt the colors and lighting to the theme, from warmth and comfort to anxiety, exhaustion, and starting over. | Example 1: Message anxiety on the commute | Example 2: Making time for yourself | |:---:|:---:| | | | | Subway station · Walking shots · Emotional close-ups | Outdoor café · Warm light · Everyday gestures | --- ### A5: Historical Cartoon Send stick figures into history: samurai on Edo streets, black cats in ancient Egyptian temples, soldiers in Roman camps. Period clothing, colorful settings, and playful contrasts make history easier to picture. - **Visual style**: solid white round heads, black oval eyes, bold clear outlines, and thin line-drawn limbs, paired with period clothing, soft cel shading, and colorful backgrounds. Change the costumes, buildings, props, and music for each place and era while keeping the same character drawing style. - **Best for**: world history, curious facts about civilizations, everyday life in the past, historical figures, and humorous history shorts. - **Choose this when**: you want to turn a fact into something a character actually experiences. Reactions and story twists help a small historical detail hold the viewer's attention. | Example 1: Edo Japan · A samurai's everyday life | Example 2: Ancient Egypt · Cats and mummies | |:---:|:---:| | | | | Edo streets · Samurai clothing · Everyday contrasts | Colorful temples · Black cat characters · History with a twist | Style and prompt contribution: [Lawal Ridwan / @leksautomate](https://github.com/leksautomate). --- ### A6: Coming soon… New specialized director styles are currently in training. [Star the project](#road-to-10000-stars--creator-ecosystem) to unlock them at 5,000 Stars! --- ## 🤖 B · Autopilot Mode style gallery Styles are numbered B1, B2, B3… Each has its own finished examples combining illustrated scenes with subtle animation, maintained separately from the A series. ### B1: Minimal Hand-Drawn Let the narration lead. Expressive stick figures, colorful hand-drawn props, and bold on-screen text make ideas, stories, and product benefits clear and engaging. - **Visual style**: near-white paper with a barely visible grid, black hand-drawn lines, and a few colorful props. Expressive faces, small animated details, flowing transitions, and sound effects keep the story moving. On-screen text highlights key ideas; captions follow the narration. - **Best for**: YouTube explainers, psychology and personal growth, workplace stories, educational videos, and product promotion. - **Choose this when**: you want a complete narrated, captioned video from a topic, copy, or story script. The visuals follow the voiceover's natural rhythm, making it a good fit for sustained explanations and long-form storytelling. Click a GIF to view or download the preview with sound.

[Star the project](#road-to-10000-stars--creator-ecosystem) to unlock them at 5,000 Stars! ## 🖼️ High-CTR Thumbnail & Publishing Kit **Your video is only as good as the click.** Once your animation is complete, orchestrate matched thumbnail art, high-CTR titles, and viewer engagement hooks in the same workflow. An integrated finishing pack for both **Director and Autopilot Mode**: generates visual hooks tailored to your video's approved character and art style, complete with ready-to-publish YouTube metadata.
A simple question and one clear symbol. A story setup with an oversized obstacle. Period costume, scenery and display lettering.
One conflict, told through extreme scale. Busy versus effective, at a glance. A relatable scene, painted light and hand lettering.
*All thumbnail concepts are designed around proven YouTube packaging psychology: bold visual contradictions, clean silhouettes, and mobile-readable typography.* ### What the kit delivers: - **1-Click Thumbnail Prompt**: Matched to your video’s exact character style, color palette, and core conflict. Ready to generate in Midjourney, Google Flow, or DALL-E. - **5 High-CTR Title Variants**: Formulated for search intent, curiosity gaps, and broad viewer appeal. - **YouTube Studio Description & SEO**: Complete with video timestamps, topic summary, and relevant tags. - **Pinned Comment Hook**: A provocative question designed to trigger viewer debates and algorithm retention. - **Pre-Publish Checklist**: Safe-zone verification for mobile, contrast check, and Content-ID readiness. ### How to trigger it: Once you approve your video script or final cut, simply send to your AI assistant: ```text Generate the Thumbnail & Publishing Kit for this video: - 1 landscape 16:9 thumbnail prompt matching the current art style - 5 viral YouTube title options + description draft - 1 engagement question for the pinned comment ``` *Outputs are production-ready to drag & drop directly into YouTube Studio or TikTok.* ## ❓ Frequently Asked Questions ### Q1. Is this really 100% free? Are there any hidden fees? Yes. Stickman Video Director is 100% free and open-source under the MIT license. You can use it freely for both personal and commercial projects. Unlike proprietary SaaS platforms that charge $30–$60/month, this project has zero subscription fees. You only pay for your own third-party API usage (e.g., Google Gemini, Claude, or ElevenLabs) based on the models you choose to connect. ### Q2. Can I monetize these videos on YouTube and TikTok? Yes, absolutely. A major concern for faceless creators is YouTube's "Reused Content" or "Low-effort AI" demonetization policy. Because Stickman Video Director writes custom storytelling arcs, unique narrative pacing, and original visual staging, your output is completely original. Hundreds of channels successfully monetize stickman narrative videos under the YouTube Partner Program (YPP). ### Q3. Do I need programming skills or an expensive GPU? No. You do not need a high-end RTX graphics card or coding knowledge. - **Director Mode** runs conversationally inside any Skill-compatible AI assistant. - **Autopilot Mode** runs inside AI coding agents (like Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor) using simple conversational English. All heavy visual generation is handled via lightweight cloud APIs or procedural rendering, not your local hardware. ### Q4. Can I make a video without an existing script? Yes. You can paste a rough idea, a shower thought, a news link, or an entire blog post. The AI director will extract the core conflict, write a compelling 3-second hook, and structure your topic into a tight 6-scene narrative arc complete with comedic timing and voiceover cues. ### Q5. When should I choose Director Mode vs. Autopilot Mode? - **Choose Director Mode** when you want absolute control over every single shot, camera angle, and visual metaphor. It acts as your cost safety net: you approve the script and storyboards for free before generating a single video frame. - **Choose Autopilot Mode** when you want a hands-off, 1-click experience that automatically generates the script, voiceover, captions, and finished video file. ### Q6. How does the AI ensure the video has high viewer retention and isn't boring? Traditional AI tools just spit out literal illustrations of text. Stickman Video Director applies real **visual storytelling psychology**: - **The 3-Second Hook**: Transforms your opening sentence into an immediate visual contradiction or curiosity gap to stop viewers from scrolling away. - **Visual Metaphors**: Converts abstract boring concepts into comedic visual jokes (e.g., anxiety depicted as a shrinking hamster wheel, burnout as a 1% battery bar). - **Pacing & Comic Pauses**: Inserts structured pauses, reaction shots, and sound effect cues (SFX) to mirror the comedic timing of creators like Casually Explained. ### Q7. What AI assistants and video editors are supported? - **AI Environments**: Compatible with Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Cursor, Antigravity, or any agent environment with file and terminal access. - **Video Generators**: Works seamlessly with Google Flow, Runway (Gen-3), Luma Dream Machine, Kling, Pika, or any image-to-video / text-to-video model. - **Video Editors**: Prompts and audio exports are ready to drag-and-drop into CapCut, Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, or Final Cut. ### Q8. What if I dislike one specific scene—do I have to re-render the whole video? No! That is the core advantage of our modular 6-scene architecture. If Scene 3 needs adjustment, you only revise that single scene prompt. Scenes 1, 2, 4, 5, and 6 remain untouched. This saves you 80% of editing time and eliminates wasted generation credits. ## ⭐ Road to 10,000 Stars & Creator Ecosystem **Every star fuels the next drop!** Together, we’re building a 100% free, open-source studio to help solo creators run faceless channels without $50/mo SaaS subscriptions. - [x] **1,000 Stars**: Shipped Director Mode + 5 core visual styles - [x] **3,000 Stars**: Shipped AutoPilot Mode for 1-click video generation - [ ] **🔥 5,000 Stars**: - 5–10 new visual styles drop - 1-click batch editor for YouTube Shorts & TikTok - [ ] **7,500 Stars**: - 1,000+ viral YouTube script prompt vault - 200+ royalty-free, Content-ID safe SFX and transitions - [ ] **10,000 Stars**: Launch the official all-in-one Web Studio

1 个用于置顶评论的互动问题 ``` *交付内容可直接用于制作与发布，拖放进 YouTube Studio 或 TikTok 即可。* ## ❓ 常见问题解答 (FAQ) ### Q1. 这真的是 100% 免费的吗？有没有隐藏收费？ 是的。Stickman Video Director 采用 MIT 开源协议，100% 完全免费且开源，你可以自由用于个人创作或商业变现。不同于传统每月收取 $30–$60 昂贵月费的商业软件，本项目没有任何订阅费。你只需根据自己选择调用的第三方大模型服务（如 Google Gemini、Claude 或 ElevenLabs）按需支付官方 API 费用。 ### Q2. 生成的视频可以在 YouTube 和 TikTok 上开通收益变现吗？ 完全可以。无脸号创作者最担心被平台判定为“搬运重复内容（Reused Content）”或“低质 AI 垃圾”导致无法获利。由于本项目生成的是具有高度原创叙事节奏、独特视觉分镜和有针对性撰写的故事脚本，成片完全属于高价值原创内容，符合 YouTube 创作者收益计划（YPP）与 TikTok 创作者基金的变现标准。 ### Q3. 我需要懂编程或者拥有昂贵的高性能显卡吗？ 完全不需要。你不需要购买几万块的专业独立显卡，也不需要懂写代码。 - **分镜导演模式（Director Mode）**：直接在任意支持 Skill 的 AI 助手对话框里用普通中文/英文交流即可使用； - **全自动模式（Autopilot Mode）**：运行在 Claude Code、Codex 或 Cursor 等现代智能体环境中，所有繁重的生成均交由云端 API 或轻量级渲染完成，不消耗本地硬件配置。 ### Q4. 如果我手里没有写好的现成剧本，能直接做视频吗？ 可以。你可以直接扔给 AI 导演一段粗糙的想法、一个新闻链接、甚至一整篇公众号长文。AI 导演会自动提炼核心戏剧冲突，写出前 3 秒爆款黄金钩子，并将你的主题拆解为带有幽默节奏与台词断句的 6 幕式标准分镜。 ### Q5. 我应该如何选择“分镜导演模式”与“全自动模式”？ - **选择分镜导演模式（Director Mode）**：当你希望严格把控每一个镜头构图、运镜轨迹和视觉隐喻时使用。它是你的“零成本安全网”，在生成任何真实视频之前，你可以完全免费地反复微调剧本和分镜； - **选择全自动模式（Autopilot Mode）**：当你追求极致出片效率、想当甩手掌柜时使用。一键自动编排剧本、对齐配音、生成字幕并合成完整成片。 ### Q6. 它是如何确保视频具有高完播率、有梗且不枯燥的？ 普通 AI 工具只会机械地把文字直译成画面，导致视频像催眠 PPT。Stickman Video Director 植入了专业的**视觉叙事心理学**： - **黄金 3 秒钩子**：将开篇第一句话重构为视觉反差或悬念冲突，瞬间抓住注意力防止观众划走； - **爆款视觉隐喻**：把枯燥抽象的概念转化为具象的搞笑视觉梗（例如把“精神内耗”具象化为一个疯狂自转的仓鼠轮，把“被掏空”具象化为头顶仅剩 1% 的低电量进度条）； - **卡点与节奏留白**：内置情绪铺垫、反转神表情与音效提示点（SFX），完美还原 Casually Explained 等顶流创作者的幽默节奏。 ### Q7. 支持哪些 AI 助手和剪辑软件？ -
